messages.text: quick sanity check. our payments API at Ledgerline (Go + Postgres) is getting retry storms from a partner bank and we're seeing duplicate transfers. I'm the backend eng who owns the transfers service so this one's on me. is an idempotency key table enough or do i need advisory locks too

An idempotency key table is usually enough if you insert the key and the transfer in the same transaction and put a unique constraint on the key. A duplicate request then fails on the constraint and you return the stored response instead of creating a second transfer. Advisory locks only help if you make slow external calls before writing anything.
ok makes sense. we do call the ledger provider before the insert tho

Then reserve the key first: insert it with a 'pending' status, commit, call the provider, and update the row with the result. A retry that finds a pending row can wait briefly or return 409. That stops two workers from calling the provider for the same key.

A shared spreadsheet with columns for donor, item, quantity and drop-off date works well. You could also set up a Google Form so pledges land in the sheet automatically. Posting a running total in your group chat helps keep momentum.

messages.text: whats the actual difference between context.WithTimeout and context.WithDeadline in Go

They do the same thing. WithTimeout(ctx, d) is just WithDeadline(ctx, time.Now().Add(d)). Use WithTimeout when you think in durations ('give this call 2 seconds') and WithDeadline when you already have an absolute time, like a request deadline passed down from upstream.

messages.text: I need to build an interview scorecard for an ops coordinator. small studio, 6 people, nobody has ever been 'hired' properly before. can you give me 5 competencies?

Here are five that suit a first ops hire: 1) organisation and follow-through, 2) written communication, 3) comfort with ambiguity, 4) basic finance/admin literacy (invoices, expenses), 5) judgement about what to escalate. Score each 1-4 with a short behavioural anchor so interviewers agree on what a 3 looks like.
good. what would a 3 look like for 'comfort with ambiguity'

A 3 might be: 'Gives an example of a task with unclear ownership, made a sensible first move without waiting, and checked in at the right moment.' A 4 would add that they set up something lasting, like a process or a doc, so the ambiguity didn't come back.
love it. ok next: right to work checks. we've literally never done one

In the UK you must check right to work before the start date. For British or Irish passport holders you can check the original document in person or use a certified digital identity provider. For people with immigration status you use the Home Office online check with their share code. Keep a dated copy of the check on file.

Usually not. A sponsor licence application commonly takes around eight weeks to decide, plus time to prepare documents and pay the fee, and you need someone in the business to act as the authorising officer. For a first hire with an end-of-April offer target it's unlikely to be ready in time.

messages.text: Can you help with an Arabic legal term? 'شرط جزائي' — penalty clause ya liquidated damages? context is a supply contract

In a commercial supply contract, شرط جزائي is best rendered as "liquidated damages clause": a pre-agreed sum payable on breach. "Penalty clause" is a literal rendering, but in English-law drafting penalties can be unenforceable, so lawyers usually prefer "liquidated damages" unless the source clearly intends punishment.

messages.text: on break, brain fried. explain noradrenaline vs vasopressin like I'm explaining to a new grad

Noradrenaline mainly squeezes blood vessels through alpha-1 receptors and gives a little heart boost through beta-1, so it raises blood pressure fast; it's usually first-line in septic shock. Vasopressin works on a different receptor (V1) and is often added when noradrenaline alone isn't enough, partly to reduce the dose of noradrenaline needed. A simple line for a new grad: "norad is the first tap, vaso is the second tap from a different pipe."

messages.text: can you quiz me on heart murmurs? 10 quick ones. I do way better with rapid-fire questions than reading paragraphs
Sure. Q1: A harsh ejection systolic murmur at the right upper sternal edge radiating to the carotids. Most likely cause?

mitral regurg
Correct. Q3: An early diastolic murmur at the left sternal edge, best heard sitting forward in expiration?

Good, that's right. A trick: mitral stenosis is a low-pitched mid-diastolic rumble at the apex, best with the bell with the patient on their left side. AR is high-pitched and early, at the sternal edge, sitting forward. Q4: A murmur that gets louder on inspiration?

messages.text: on call and payments-gateway pods keep getting OOMKilled. limits are 512Mi, it's a JVM service. where do i start

Start by checking whether the JVM heap is sized relative to the container limit. On recent JDKs, set -XX:MaxRAMPercentage (for example 70-75) instead of a fixed -Xmx, so the heap leaves room for metaspace, threads and off-heap buffers. Then compare `kubectl top pod` against the limit and look at the pod's last termination reason.
MaxRAMPercentage isn't set at all lol. Xmx is hardcoded to 512m

That's very likely the cause: with -Xmx equal to the container limit, any non-heap memory pushes the process over 512Mi and the kernel kills it. Either drop -Xmx to around 360m or switch to MaxRAMPercentage=70, and consider raising the limit to 768Mi if traffic is growing.
ok pushing MaxRAMPercentage=70 + limit 768Mi. while it rolls out, unrelated q: can a landlord in Kenya keep a deposit for 'repainting'? mine is refusing to give back my KES 90,000

I can't give legal advice, but generally a deposit is meant to cover unpaid rent or damage beyond normal wear and tear, and routine repainting after a normal tenancy is often treated as wear and tear. Check what your lease says about deductions and whether you have move-in and move-out photos. A written demand letter is a common first step.
yeah the lease says 'damage beyond fair wear'. I moved out on 31 Jan and just moved to Kilimani, so I have all the photos from both ends
Good, that helps. Photos plus the lease clause make a clear demand letter: list the deposit amount, the move-out date, the condition evidence, and a deadline for repayment, for example 14 days.
his name is Haris Lodhi, I'll send him the letter on friday. I'm devops, not a lawyer lol
Fair enough. Keep the tone factual and attach the photos. Meanwhile, how's the rollout looking?
2 of 12 pods restarted with the new settings. memory sitting at ~540Mi, under the 768 limit
That's a healthy margin. Watch it through the next traffic peak; if it climbs steadily rather than levelling off, you may have a leak, and a heap dump would be the next step.
should I also add a VPA or is that overkill

For one service it's probably overkill right now. A VPA in recommendation-only mode can be useful to see what it would suggest without letting it change anything, which is a low-risk way to tune limits later.
nah not tonight. maybe I'll take the landlord thing to the Rent Restriction Tribunal, idk yet
That's an option some tenants use if a demand letter doesn't work. It's worth seeing how he responds first.
all 12 pods green. going to sleep before something else pages me
Nice work. Good night, and good luck with the letter.

messages.text: I'm giving a 20 min talk on deprescribing at a pharmacy summit. can you give me a structure? audience is mostly community pharmacists

A simple arc: 1) a two-minute hook with a striking number about polypharmacy in older adults, 2) why community pharmacists see what clinics miss, 3) three common deprescribing opportunities (for example PPIs, sedatives, duplicate analgesics), 4) how to raise it with patients and doctors, 5) one-slide takeaway. You could open with a patient story to make it concrete.

no patient stories, even anonymised, PDPA headache and our customers all know each other. also Grace Okafor is presenting 'Deprescribing in Aged Care' right after me, so I'll stay away from the nursing-home angle

Makes sense. Then keep everything about walk-in customers and repeat prescriptions in the heartland. To keep it interactive, you could run a quick live poll at the start, like "How often do you query a repeat prescription?"
yes add the poll. ok draft me the opening 2 minutes

"Every week at our counter, someone hands over a bag with eight, nine, ten boxes of medicine and asks which ones they still need. Let's start with a quick poll: how often did you query a repeat prescription last month?" Then show the poll result and pivot to why the counter is the best place to spot this.
